title: Derivative of a rotated Gaussian distribution function
statement: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density. For every $t,y\in\mathbb R$, the function $\theta\mapsto\Phi\bigl((t-y\sin\theta)/\cos\theta\bigr)-\Phi(t)$ is differentiable at $0$, with derivative $-\varphi(t)y$.
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ denote the standard Gaussian distribution function and density. For $t,y\in\mathbb R$, define $q_{t,y}(\theta)=\Phi((t-\sin\theta\,y)/\cos\theta)-\Phi(t)$. For every $t,y$, $q_{t,y}'(0)=-\varphi(t)y$.
